To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the action of combined magnetic fields (static + alternating) on the aqueous solution (without electrodes) of amino acid glutamic acid results in the appearance of the peaks with half-width 0.5 Hz at the alternating magnetic fields frequencies equal to the cyclotronic frequency of glutamic acid ion.

(1) the current through aqueous solutions of glutamic acid is increased in the presence of combined static and alternating parallel magnetic fields; (2) the current increase is most prominent at the alternating magnetic frequency equal to the corresponding cyclotron frequency; (3) the effects are not observed at the absence of the electrodes in the solution; (4) the effects are reproducible in the majority of experiments; and (5) the effects appear after 40 min. after solution preparation.

the combined static and alternating magnetic fields can cause an increase in current through an aqueous solution of a glutamic acid, and the effect can be explained on the basis of the modern quantum electrodinamics.
